vulnerability_analysis: The approve() function in the BNRG contract sets the allowance directly without checking for the race condition. When a victim calls approve() to reduce allowance from X to Y, a spender can front-run with transferFrom(X) before the reduction, then after reduction still has Y allowance. This allows stealing X+Y tokens instead of max(X,Y). The exploit requires: 1) Victim approves attacker for initial amount X, 2) Victim tries to reduce to Y, 3) Attacker front-runs with transferFrom(X), 4) Reduction sets allowance to Y, 5) Attacker uses remaining Y allowance.
attack_strategy: Simulate the race condition in a single block by controlling transaction ordering. We'll act as both victim (owner) and attacker. Steps: 1) Impersonate owner to set state to Unlocked, 2) Owner approves attacker for initial amount X, 3) Owner tries to reduce approval to Y, 4) Attacker front-runs reduction with transferFrom(X), 5) Reduction executes setting allowance to Y, 6) Attacker uses remaining Y allowance.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner to unlock contract state. 2. Owner approves attacker for 1000 tokens. 3. Owner calls approve again to reduce to 500 tokens. 4. Before reduction executes, attacker calls transferFrom for 1000 tokens. 5. Reduction executes, setting allowance to 500. 6. Attacker calls transferFrom again for 500 tokens. 7. Verify attacker balance increased by 1500 tokens.
